statements.status_notes: CVE-2012-0039 is the predictable g_str_hash collision DoS, disputed by upstream since 2012: g_hash_table_new callers can supply any hash function appropriate for their input, so the existence of g_str_hash is not a library vulnerability, and Debian marks it unimportant with no fix planned. In this image libglib2.0-0t64 2.84.4-3~deb13u3 is installed only as a shared-library dependency for conda packages that link GLib (alongside libsm6/libxext6/libxrender1); no shipped component runs a service that feeds untrusted network input into GLib hash tables. The entrypoint is a bash passthrough (exec "$@") with default cmd /bin/bash, so there is no execution path where an adversary controls hash-table keys.

CVE-2012-0039 is the predictable g_str_hash collision DoS, disputed by upstream since 2012: g_hash_table_new callers can supply any hash function appropriate for their input, so the existence of g_str_hash is not a library vulnerability, and Debian marks it unimportant with no fix planned. In this image libglib2.0-0t64 2.84.4-3~deb13u3 is installed only as a shared-library dependency for conda packages that link GLib (alongside libsm6/libxext6/libxrender1); no shipped component runs a service that feeds untrusted network input into GLib hash tables. The entrypoint is a bash passthrough (exec "$@") with default cmd /bin/bash, so there is no execution path where an adversary controls hash-table keys.

Disputed by vendor. The existence of the g_str_hash function is not a vulnerability in the library, because callers of g_hash_table_new and g_hash_table_new_full can specify an arbitrary hash function that is appropriate for the application.
